name: Sun
description: The Sun is a G-type main-sequence star at the centre of the Solar System. It holds 99.8% of the system's mass and governs the orbits of every planet, moon, and small body.

name: Mercury
description: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun. A cratered, airless world, it completes an 88-day orbit with days longer than its year.

name: Venus
description: Venus is a rocky planet wrapped in a thick carbon-dioxide atmosphere. Surface temperatures are high enough to melt lead, hotter than Mercury despite the greater distance from the Sun.

name: Earth
description: Earth is the only known world with liquid-water oceans and life. A 23.4° axial tilt and a 24-hour rotation give rise to seasons and a protective magnetic field.

name: Moon
description: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite, tidally locked so the same face always points home. Its dry, cratered surface still carries the marks of Apollo landings.

name: Mars
description: Mars is a cold desert planet with the tallest volcano and the longest canyon in the Solar System. Polar ice and ancient riverbeds hint at a wetter past.

name: Jupiter
description: Jupiter is the largest planet, a hydrogen-helium giant with a faint ring system. The Great Red Spot is an anticyclone wider than Earth, and four large Galilean moons orbit nearby.

name: Saturn
description: Saturn is a gas giant known for its broad, icy ring system. Low density and a hexagonal storm at the north pole set it apart from the other giants.

name: Uranus
description: Uranus is an ice giant that rolls on its side, with an axial tilt of about 82°. Methane in the atmosphere gives the planet its pale cyan colour.

name: Neptune
description: Neptune is the most distant planet, an ice giant with the strongest winds in the Solar System. The Great Dark Spot seen by Voyager 2 has since faded and reformed.

name: Ganymede
description: Ganymede is the largest moon in the Solar System, bigger than Mercury. An iron core and a likely subsurface ocean make it the only moon with its own magnetic field.

name: Titan
description: Titan is Saturn's largest moon and the only satellite with a dense atmosphere. Lakes and rivers of liquid methane run across a water-ice crust.

name: Callisto
description: Callisto is the outermost Galilean moon, a heavily cratered ice-rock body. It is the most geologically quiet of Jupiter's large moons.

name: Io
description: Io is the most volcanically active body in the Solar System. Jupiter's tides flex its interior, feeding hundreds of sulfur volcanoes.

name: Europa
description: Europa is an ice-covered moon with a young, fractured crust. A global ocean of liquid water is thought to lie beneath, making it a prime target in the search for life.

name: Triton
description: Triton is Neptune's largest moon and orbits backwards relative to Neptune's spin. Nitrogen geysers and a captured, Pluto-like composition suggest it was once a Kuiper Belt object.
